e: From 1700s British hooray or hurray, affected by h-dropping. Alternately, may come from Thurawal uru.
q: I used to hear people say ‘ooroo’ when I was young (in Adelaide) but haven’t heard it for decades.
Grandma used to say it all the time - ooroo.
The ’roo has jumped away, leaving its iconic outline, along with the ‘see you later’ meaning of the traditional phrase ‘ooroo’.
